scope: Proposition 7.1 of the manuscript “Relative denominators and effective systems for log Calabi-Yau fibrations” (preprints/Relative-denominators-and-effective-systems-for-log-Calabi-Yau-fibrations-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 034 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a539053eb28e6c4d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix an integer 1 ≤ d ≤ 4, a DCC set I ⊂ [0, 1] ∩ Q, and a positive integer p. There exists a positive integer ℓ = ℓ(d, I, p) with the following property. Let Z be a normal projective complex variety of dimension d with a rationally connected smooth projective resolution. Suppose that (Z, B + MZ) is generalized klt, that B ≥ 0 has coefficients in I, and that the b-nef rational b-divisor M has pM b-Cartier. If D = KZ + B + MZ ∼Q 0, then ℓD is an integral principal divisor. Consequently, for every integer a ≥ 1, the divisor aℓD is principal and h0 Z, OZ(aℓD)  = 1. The same integer can be chosen for all dimensions in any fixed subset of {1, 2, 3, 4}.
